title: Return of the Heroes - A Hidden Gem, or a Game Best Forgotten?
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_EZK5vA1EX0

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at *Return of the Heroes*, an overland adventure game that reads as a relic of the 1980s and is in fact from 2004. The framing is a warning as much as a review: when an obscure old game surfaces in the Dungeon Dive Facebook group, excitement runs ahead of evidence and eBay prices run from thirty to a hundred dollars. Not everything old is a hidden gem. Forty dollars, he suggests, is the sensible ceiling.

The rulebook is historically terrible — rules split across an introductory setup, a rulebook, a glossary and a condensed sheet, and written as a conversation between characters, which he finds charming and genuinely obstructive. The glossary, an alphabetical index of every encounter and chit, he singles out as something more games of this type should copy.

The game itself is a fetch-quest overland crawl beside *Talisman*, *Prophecy* and *Runebound*, with roll-under stat tests, sixteen rearrangeable tiles, and quest tokens drawn from a bag onto fixed coordinates — random enough to vary, fixed enough that the world acquires a history. He plays with house rules to speed it up, thins the bag and adds the Nameless One's generals to compensate. He draws a direct line from this to *Explor*, and calls it a decent gateway to the better game.

----

How much house-ruling is fair game before you are no longer playing the designer's game at all?
